{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ne-o","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"d8c14dbe202d65209fb99724a9ade3a6d694a7b4c27f4028c157967b4bdafa5c","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ne-class-o:lineage:66","source_registry_sha256":"66161d94cc863d3cf353417f54f101bf8681de71fc4c3b73f43c86f2be1c7398","source_liveness_sha256":"78587b1f8f8617c7b8b0a43b3f0679698b900b7d64ddfc387c1773ac070571e8"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Sharing the road with riders, pedestrians and large vehicles","heading":"Sharing the road with riders, pedestrians and large vehicles","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Sharing the road with riders, pedestrians and large vehicles

FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A76
Motorcycles have the same roadway rights and privileges as other vehicles. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A76
Give a motorcycle a full lane rather than driving alongside it within the same lane. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A76
A motorcycle's small profile can make it harder to see and to judge its approach speed or distance. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A76
Signal before merging or changing lanes so riders can anticipate the traffic movement. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A76
Check mirrors and blind areas for motorcycles before changing lanes and at intersections. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A76
Do not assume a rider will turn merely because the motorcycle's indicator is flashing; wait for confirmation of the maneuver. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A76
Expect riders to alter speed or lane position for gravel, potholes, slick surfaces, seams, rail crossings or grooved pavement. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A76
The handbook recommends a three-to-four-second following gap behind a motorcycle for maneuvering and emergency stopping. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A76
In dry conditions, a motorcycle can stop faster than a car. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A76
Under the printed bicycle rule, riders have motor-vehicle drivers' rights and duties and must follow traffic laws. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A76
Bicyclists generally ride as far right as practical within a lane or on a paved shoulder. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A76
A bicyclist may occupy the travel lane where it is too narrow for a bicycle and motor vehicle to share safely side by side. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A77
A bicyclist may change lanes for a left turn or to continue through an intersection rather than remaining in the right lane. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A77
On an urban one-way street, bicyclists may use the far-left lane. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A77
Expect cyclists to move within a lane to avoid road-surface hazards. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A77
Before a right turn, merge with bicycle traffic rather than turning directly across a same-direction cyclist's path. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A77
For a left turn, yield to an approaching cyclist just as to an approaching motor vehicle. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A77
Avoid a horn blast when approaching a bicyclist, and check for bicycles before opening a vehicle door. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A77
When applicable, overtaking a same-direction bicycle requires a safe clearance of at least three feet maintained until safely past. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A77
If a safe three-foot bicycle-passing clearance is unavailable, reduce speed and wait for a safe opportunity. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A77
Children can unexpectedly ride into a road midblock from a driveway, alley or curb without looking or stopping. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F22 | anchor: A77
Swerving or riding against traffic may indicate an inexperienced cyclist and calls for added precautions. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F23 | anchor: A77
Before turning, look both ways for cyclists using sidewalks or trails parallel to the road. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F24 | anchor: A77
At intersections and roundabouts, the same right-of-way rules apply to bicycles and motor vehicles. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F25 | anchor: A77
Anticipate pedestrians anywhere, especially midblock near homes, parks and schools, and be ready to yield. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F26 | anchor: A77
Watch for pedestrians who misjudge signals or cross against a light. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F27 | anchor: A77
Yield to pedestrians while turning and use special care where red-light turns are permitted. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F28 | anchor: A77
At a stop sign or red light, stop completely behind a crosswalk whether it is marked or unmarked. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F29 | anchor: A77
Do not pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian because it may conceal the person crossing. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec14-F30 | anchor: A77
Stop and remain stopped for a blind or visually impaired person using a white cane or service dog until the person is clear of the road. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> pdf-0077]

Misconceptions: A motorcycle needs its own lane; an active school-bus stop arm differs from amber pre-stop lights; seeing a truck mirror is not proof that its driver is watching.
Mnemonics: See the smaller user, leave room, check the blind area, respect the stop.
Glossary: A No-Zone is a truck or bus blind/space-conflict area; amber bus lights warn of a coming stop; a truck apron accommodates large vehicles' rear wheels.
Dynamic facts: Live contact details, services and variable fees are withheld from this stable inventory.
